IMPROVE collects ways to support yourself while moving through distress.

## Imagery {#imagery}

Imagine a relaxing scene, a protected room, a calming fantasy, events going well, painful emotion draining away, or a happy time that you can replay in your mind.

## Meaning {#meaning}

Look for purpose or a positive aspect within the painful situation. Repeat what you find, or connect the moment with spiritual or personal values.

## Prayer {#prayer}

Open your heart to a supreme being, God, your own Wise Mind, or whatever fits your beliefs. Ask for strength to bear the pain or practise turning over what you cannot control.

## Relaxation {#relaxation}

Use a warm bath, a hot drink, massage, stretching, yoga, deep breathing, or a deliberately relaxed facial expression.

## One Thing in the Moment {#one-thing-in-the-moment}

Put your full attention on exactly what you are doing now. Return your mind to the present and to the physical sensations of this one moment.

## Vacation {#vacation}

Take a brief, time-limited break from responsibility: rest in bed, spend time outside, read something enjoyable, turn off your phone, or give yourself an hour away from hard work. Choose a break that will not create a larger problem later.

## Self-Encouragement {#self-encouragement}

Speak to yourself as you would to someone you care about. Examples from the handout include: *I will make it out of this*, *I am doing the best I can*, *I can stand it*, *This too shall pass*, and *It will not last forever*. Add rethoughts that are especially useful in your own crisis situations.
